class.description: core/profile class identity, e.g. port, psu, fan, blank

conforms.description: standards-registry key; size is lint-enforced against schemas/standards.yaml

interface.description: this component IS a receptacle presenting this mating interface, e.g. sfp, qsfp, rj45, iec-c14. Occupants declare the same key via `mates`. Deliberately not an enum - a new interface is a new key, not a schema change.

mates.description: this component mates INTO a receptacle presenting this interface. Requires a `mate` connection-point, which is what aligns it to its host.

body.description: 3D body for FRU modules: box depth behind the face; per-side art via skins/body-{left,right,top,bottom,rear}.svg, each drawn as photographed from outside that side (right: face at image left; left: face at image right; rear as seen from behind)

color.description: side color where no art exists

travel.description: captive module: pulls out this far and stays in the chassis (omit for removable FRUs)

footprint.description: body box smaller than the face (mounting tabs exist only on the thin faceplate)

plate.description: faceplate slab bounds (defaults to the full face) - trim to the art so no bare plate edge shows

relief.description: 3D interior model: cavity wall color, cavity shape node and cross-section, and per-node features

cavity.description: skin node id whose bbox is the recess; default = whole component

size.description: cavity cross-section bbox in mm; default = the aperture (size). Set when the opening steps in - the aperture is the hole in the panel, the cavity is the box behind it.

round.description: cavity is circular: shape-punched from the cavity node's art, cylindrical walls

source.description: where precisely, in one phrase - the part a `borrowed` figure came from, the figure a `drawing` one was read off, the photograph behind a `photo-measured` one. The machine-readable half is `confidence`; this is the half that lets the next reader go and check, and it is what stops twenty features sharing one reading from reading as twenty readings.

top.description: mm the feature rises above the cavity floor

sink.description: mm the feature recesses beyond the cavity floor

out.description: mm the feature protrudes outward from the panel face

dome.description: domed LED: apex protrudes this many mm, rim slightly inset

cyl.description: cylindrical protrusion this many mm tall (radius from the node's bbox); combine with lift to stack

bar.description: round tube of this diameter lying along the node's long axis, spanning lift..lift+bar off the face (U-handle crossbars)

uhandle.description: complete U-shaped tube handle this many mm proud: legs at the node's long-axis ends, continuous 90-degree bends, crossbar; tube diameter = node's short axis

lift.description: standoff: the feature starts this many mm off the face (floating handle bars, stacked washers)

knurl.description: knurled side surface (thumbscrews) - rendered as fine grip ridges around a cyl

thread.description: threaded side surface - value is the thread pitch in mm (e.g. 1/4-36 UNS = 25.4/36 = 0.706). Rendered as a single-start helix around a cyl. Use instead of knurl for coax bushings and screw barrels.

vent.description: air vent: the node's dark cells become real holes into a cavity this deep

size-confidence.description: where each of w/h/d came from, per dimension. Keyed by dimension ON PURPOSE: a part can have a measured width and an impossible depth, and one scalar could not say that. Absent means unstated, which is what most of the library is; the component index counts the gap so it cannot go quiet.

size-notes.description: one phrase per the `source` convention - what rules a known-wrong value out, or where a sourced one came from. The long argument belongs in provenance; this is the pointer beside the number.

insert.description: the envelope a bay must reserve, in mm, when it differs from `size`. `size` is what the skin DRAWS - the faceplate as depicted. `insert` is what the slot has to accommodate, which on a card with ejector brackets is longer than the plate: Cisco states both, sometimes in one sheet ('Physical dimensions (includes ejector bracket/lever)') and sometimes without saying which it means. Absent means the two are the same, which is the common case. Never a guess: state it only where a source gives both figures, and say in provenance which is which.

attrs.description: default data-* attributes for instances. Free-form, except that the power figures below are typed: they are the terms of a sum, and a term that is a string is not a number no matter how it reads

power-draw-typical-w.description: load this module IMPOSES in normal operation. Draw and supply are opposite signs of one unit and must never share a key: summing a chassis's `watts` over two PSUs and eight line cards yields a plausible number that is neither

power-draw-max-w.description: load at its worst rated case. Where a vendor states one figure per ambient - Cisco gives 25/40/55 C per card - this is the highest, which is what `max` means

power-draw-min-w.description: load at idle, with nothing populated

power-output-w.description: continuous output this module is rated to PROVIDE - a PSU or a power-entry module. Deliberately not `power-output-max-w`: draw has a distribution and supply has a rating, and a symmetric name would advertise a `power-output-typical-w` that means nothing

power-draw-scope.description: WHAT the power-draw-* figures on this contract cover. Absent means `module` - this module and nothing else - so every figure written before this key existed keeps meaning exactly what it meant. `module-with-paired-io` is for a vendor who measures the pair and publishes no bare figure: Casa heads its C100G table 'Maximum consumption WITH I/O module' and gives the same US16x8 200 W or 220 W depending on which rear module it sits behind, so a bare-card figure may not exist to be divided out. The scope is DATA and not a provenance sentence because it changes the arithmetic: a consumer summing a chassis must not add the rear partner of a card already scoped to include it, and a consumer asking what one card draws must be able to see that the answer contains another card. A prose note is true, well written, and invisible to both of them

elements.description: contracted sub-elements; key = element segment id

at.description: mm offset from component origin (top-left, y-down)

description.description: the vendor's own sentence about this element, kept beside the state tokens - never instead of them

parts.description: sub-components composed into this component (compile-time flattened); e.g. a std/ cutout core inside a bezel

lift.description: mm this composed part sits proud of the parent's face. Use when the parent itself protrudes (a transceiver body, a raised bezel) and the part's cavity should recess from THAT surface rather than from the panel.

states.description: states of the component as a whole

bays.description: for modules that themselves host bays (v0: unused)

watts.description: watts, as a number. `watts: '650'` was a string, and that is not cosmetic: '650' + '400' is '650400' in more than one language a consumer might use, and max('650', '1600') is '650' in all of them

behavior.description: how the lamp is lit, as opposed to what colour it is lit. Omitted means solid. A state is colour AND behaviour: solid green and blinking green are different facts on real hardware. The object form takes a second `color` for `alternating`, and exists so that a blink `rate` can be added later as one more property rather than a coercion

color.description: the second colour, for `alternating` - the lamp flashes between `color` and this one
LED color for this state, emitted as scoped CSS

d.description: recess depth behind the panel face in mm (3D); optional

confidence.description: where a NUMBER came from. One vocabulary for the library, shared by relief features and by size-confidence: measured (off this part's own hardware), photo-measured, drawing (off this part's own artwork or a vendor figure of it), datasheet, registry (from standards.yaml), borrowed (another Portrayal part's MEASURED figure for the same class of hardware, reused because nobody publishes one for this part - an estimate, but not a free one, and `source` must name the part), estimated (a plausible figure with no source), and `known-wrong`. KNOWN-WRONG IS THE TERMINAL STATE AND IT IS NOT A CONFIDENCE LEVEL: it says the value is not merely unmeasured but IMPOSSIBLE - contradicted by something checkable - and is being carried only because removing it would break the model and no sourced replacement exists. A value that cannot be true must not sit in the same bucket as one nobody has measured. `source` must say what rules it out. Note the enum omits standards.yaml's `verified`, which answers a different question - whether a CUTOUT matches its governing standard.
